title: The Enormous Turnip
text:
An old man planted a turnip, and it grew and grew until it was enormous. When it was time to harvest, the old man took hold of the leaves and pulled. He pulled and pulled, but the turnip did not move.

He called the old woman. She took hold of the old man, and the old man took hold of the turnip, and they pulled and pulled, but they could not pull it up.

The old woman called their granddaughter. The granddaughter took hold of the old woman, the old woman of the old man, the old man of the turnip. They pulled and pulled, and still nothing.

The granddaughter called the dog. The dog took hold of the granddaughter, and they all pulled together, but the turnip stayed in the ground. The dog called the cat, and the cat joined the line, and they pulled once more without success.

Finally the cat called the mouse. The mouse took hold of the cat, the cat of the dog, the dog of the granddaughter, the granddaughter of the old woman, the old woman of the old man, and the old man of the turnip. They pulled and pulled, and out came the turnip.
lesson: Big tasks often succeed only when everyone adds a share, and the last small contribution can make the difference. Keep calling in help, and never scorn the smallest helper.
people: Grandfather, grandmother, granddaughter, dog, cat, mouse
source: Alexander Afanasyev, Russian Folk Tales (Narodnye russkie skazki), The Turnip (Repka)
